name: Heron r2
highlight: 156-qubit heavy-hex chip with tunable couplers; IBM's 100x100 challenge machine for circuits up to 5,000 two-qubit gates.
note: IBM's announcement gives no median two-qubit error for Heron r2.

name: Heron r3 (ibm_pittsburgh)
highlight: Third Heron revision; ibm_pittsburgh launched with a median two-qubit error near 1.5e-3.
note: Error comes from a public calibration dashboard snapshot and changes over time; not an IBM spec sheet.

name: Nighthawk
highlight: Square-lattice chip with 218 tunable couplers, built for quantum advantage at up to 5,000 two-qubit gates.
note: IBM said it would reach users by the end of 2025.

name: Nighthawk r2
highlight: Adds on-chip qubit reset (458 quantum elements in all) for 100,000+ circuits per second and 7,500+ gate circuits.
note: 120 programmable qubits; 458 counts qubits, couplers and reset elements together. Blog dated 31 Aug 2026; deployed September 2026.

name: Loon
highlight: Experimental chip showing the parts of IBM's qLDPC fault-tolerant design: long-range c-couplers, multi-layer routing and qubit reset.
note: IBM gave no qubit count.

name: Nighthawk r3
highlight: Planned for 2027: 520 programmable qubits and 10,000 two-qubit operations, with l-couplers to link two chips into 1,040 qubits.
note: Announced at IBM QDC 2026; 2,034 physical elements per chip.

name: Willow
fidelity_text: mean CZ error 0.33% (chip 1); mean iSWAP-like error 0.14% (chip 2)
highlight: First below-threshold surface-code demo: logical error halved going from distance 3 to 5 to 7.
source_name: Google Quantum AI Willow spec sheet
note: Fidelity converted from chip 1's mean CZ error; chip 2 uses a different gate.

name: Majorana 1
highlight: First chip built on Microsoft's topological-core design: eight qubits on a chip designed to scale to a million.
note: Physicists dispute whether topological qubits have been shown; no gate fidelity has been published.

name: Ocelot
highlight: Cat-qubit prototype: 5 cat data qubits, 5 buffer circuits and 4 error-detecting qubits; AWS says it can cut error-correction cost by up to 90%.
note: qubits = 5 cat data qubits + 4 ancilla qubits (14 core components including buffers).

name: Forte Enterprise
highlight: IonQ's 2024 data-center trapped-ion generation; 36-qubit class before Tempo.
note: Figures are the roadmap's 2024 row, not a Forte Enterprise spec sheet; month is a placeholder.

name: Tempo
highlight: Reached #AQ 64, the highest validated algorithmic-qubit score, three months ahead of schedule.
note: IonQ's own blog describes a 64-qubit computational register on the Tempo development system; QCR calls it a 100-qubit system.

name: EQC test chip (99.99% 2Q)
highlight: Record two-qubit gate fidelity on a chip made in a standard fab, using electronic qubit control without ground-state cooling.
note: Benchmark on one qubit pair, not a full system.

name: Superion 256
highlight: First Superion system: 256 trapped-ion qubits on electronic qubit control chips, orderable now with deliveries planned for 2027.
note: No system fidelity stated; coverage cites IonQ's 99.99% Oct 2025 record.

name: H2 (56 qubits)
highlight: Second-generation racetrack trap; upgraded from 32 to 56 qubits.
note: Launched 2023 (per Quantinuum prospectus) with 32 qubits; the month and the 2024 upgrade date come from prior knowledge.

name: Helios
highlight: 98 fully connected barium-ion qubits; 48 error-corrected logical qubits at 2:1 encoding and 94 error-detected logical qubits in a GHZ state.

name: Cepheus-1-36Q
highlight: Four 9-qubit chiplets; the largest multi-chip quantum computer when deployed in 2025.
note: Month from prior knowledge; the release says only 2025.

name: Cepheus-1-108Q
fidelity_text: median 2Q fidelity 99.5% (99.1% at GA in April 2026)
highlight: Twelve 9-qubit chiplets; reached the 99.5% median two-qubit milestone in late 2026.
note: 99.6% on an 80-qubit sublattice and 99.7% on a 50-qubit sublattice.

name: Advantage2
highlight: 4,400+ qubit annealer with 20-way Zephyr connectivity, twice the coherence and 40% higher energy scale.
note: Annealing qubits; not comparable with gate-model qubit counts.

name: DR17 / Seeker (17-qubit dual-rail)
highlight: First gate-model system from D-Wave's Quantum Circuits acquisition: 17 dual-rail qubits, planned for 2026.
note: 17-qubit Seeker named in Next Platform (Jan 2026); the 99.9% figure is from D-Wave's June 2026 roadmap release and is error-detected, so it is not used as a raw fidelity.

name: Aqumen Seeker
highlight: 8 dual-rail cavity qubits with built-in error detection.
note: D-Wave announced it was buying Quantum Circuits in January 2026 ($550M). No fidelity figures were published.

name: Omega chipset
highlight: Manufacturable silicon-photonics chipset made at GlobalFoundries, the building block for PsiQuantum's utility-scale machines.
note: Fusion is a measurement in photonic fusion-based QC, not a gate; it is left out of two_qubit_fidelity. Date from the Feb 2025 release.

name: Aurora
highlight: 12-qubit modular photonic machine: 35 chips in 4 networked server racks with 13 km of fibre, running at room temperature.

name: Aquila
highlight: 256-atom analog (Hamiltonian simulation) machine, on Amazon Braket since 2022.
note: Analog mode, no gates. The month comes from prior knowledge.

name: Gemini
highlight: Digital gate-based neutral-atom system and error-correction testbed installed with Japan's ABCI-Q supercomputer.
note: QuEra says 'launched 2025'; the month is a placeholder.

name: 200-qubit system (Saudi Arabia)
highlight: 200-qubit neutral-atom system launched for cloud access in Saudi Arabia in H1 2026; a 140-qubit system was also deployed in Italy.
note: The filing says only H1 2026, so the month is approximate. No fidelity reported.

name: 1,024-atom register
highlight: Defect-free arrays of 1,024 atoms (up from 506), with atom lifetimes about 40 times longer on a new cryogenic platform.
note: These are trapped atoms in a register, not a QPU offered to users. The month is approximate.

name: Level 2 logical-qubit machine
highlight: Record 24 entangled logical qubits; 28 logical qubits made from 112 physical atoms ran an error-corrected computation.
note: Available to order for delivery in 2025. The total physical qubit count is not stated.

name: Magne
highlight: 50-logical-qubit Level 2 machine for Denmark's QuNorth, expected to start work around the end of 2026.
note: Atom Computing's own release says 'over 1,200' physical qubits; QCR gives 1,225.

name: Sqale
highlight: Neutral-atom system that entangled 30 logical qubits made from 80 physical qubits (Sept 2026).
note: The site lists 100+ physical qubits; the 30-logical demo used 80.

name: Emerald
highlight: 54-qubit square-lattice chip with tunable couplers, generally available on IQM Resonance and Amazon Braket.

name: Halocene
highlight: Error-correction product line; the first 150-qubit system supports research on up to five logical qubits.
note: IQM said it would be commercially available by the end of 2026. 99.7% is a target.

name: Helium 2
highlight: 12-cat-qubit processor holding multi-hour bit-flip lifetimes on several qubits at once.
note: No two-qubit gate fidelity yet; bias-preserving CNOTs are the next step.

name: Toshiko
highlight: 32-qubit Gen-1 system deployed in commercial data centres in London and Tokyo.
note: Secondary source with approximate figures; the year is 2023 and the month is a placeholder.

name: Origin Wukong
highlight: China's third-generation superconducting computer, built on a 72-qubit chip; online January 2024.

name: Origin Wukong-180
highlight: Fourth-generation machine on a single-core 180-qubit chip, online 9 May 2026.
note: No fidelity reported.

name: 256-qubit superconducting computer
highlight: 256-qubit machine built on the 2023 64-qubit system, with high-density packaging inside one dilution refrigerator.
note: No fidelity reported.

name: IBEX Q1
highlight: 12-qubit fully connected trapped-ion system on Amazon Braket, the first trapped-ion QPU hosted in the EU.
note: This is an average, not a median.

name: LYNX Series
highlight: New 19-inch rack-mounted trapped-ion generation that reached Quantum Volume 32,768.
note: First units go to partners in Q4 2026. The qubit count is not stated.

name: Belenos
highlight: Second-generation 12-qubit photonic computer on the cloud; Quandela claims about 4,000 times the power of its 6-qubit predecessor.

name: Single-mode GKP bosonic qubit
highlight: Grid-state (GKP) bosonic qubit in one cavity, with SPAM error below 0.1%, about 100 times better than earlier GKP results.
note: One cavity encodes one error-corrected qubit, so physical and logical counts are both 1.

name: 4-qubit bosonic system
fidelity_text: ~three nines for single-cavity and two-qubit operations
highlight: Four-qubit bosonic system due to start operating in 2026, with an error-correction gain above 2.
note: Figures are from an executive interview, not a datasheet.

name: T-centre modules (inter-module entanglement)
highlight: Entangled T-centre spin qubits in separate cryostats over telecom fibre and ran a teleported CNOT between modules.
note: No fidelity or rate figures given; qubits = the two entangled T-centre qubits.

name: Zuchongzhi 3.0
highlight: 105-qubit processor with 182 couplers; its random-circuit-sampling result was a PRL cover article.
note: Paper: PRL 134, 090601 (2025). Single-qubit 99.90%, readout 99.13%, T1 72 us.

target: Kookaburra: first Starling module combining a logical processing unit and quantum memory
note: No qubit count given; QDC 2026 coverage did not report its status.
